does: Cooks small pasta in a thick soup instead of in a separate pot of water, adding hot liquid a little at a time, so that the starch it lets go thickens the soup into a creamy whole.

intro.what: Small pasta is cooked in the soup itself, with hot liquid added as it is drunk up.
intro.why: The starch stays in the pot and binds pasta and broth together, the way home cooks in Naples make pasta with beans, potatoes or peas.
intro.idea: Let the starch thicken the soup

how: Bring the soup to a lively simmer and keep a pan of hot liquid at hand.
Add the pasta and stir often, scraping the bottom, since the soup is thick and catches.
Add a little hot liquid whenever the pot looks dry.
Stop when the pasta is tender with a little bite and the soup is dense but still pours. It thickens as it stands.

cues.text: The soup is creamy and dense, and slowly settles when spooned.
The pasta is tender with a little bite at the centre.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the pot unstirred, so that the pasta sticks and burns on the bottom.
mistakes.fix: Stir often and scrape the bottom of the pot.

mistakes.mistake: Adding cold liquid, which stops the cooking and makes the pasta soft outside and hard inside.
Cooking it until it is thick enough to stand, so that it turns to paste on the plate.
mistakes.fix: Stop while it still pours; it thickens as it rests.

quiz.question: Why cook the pasta in the soup rather than in water?
choices: So that its starch thickens the soup.
So that the soup stays thin and clear.
So that the pasta cooks faster.
quiz.because: The starch stays in the pot and binds the soup.

quiz.question: What liquid do you add as the pasta drinks up the soup?
choices: Hot liquid, a little at a time.
quiz.because: Hot liquid keeps the pot at a simmer.

quiz.question: When is it ready?
choices: When the soup stands in a lump.
When the pasta is still hard.
When the pasta has a little bite and the soup still pours.
quiz.because: It thickens more as it stands.

quiz.question: The pasta stuck and burnt on the bottom. What would you change next time?
choices: Stir more often and add hot liquid when it looks dry.
Add the pasta to cold soup.
quiz.because: A thick soup needs stirring and liquid to keep from catching.

comes_after.why: Knowing when pasta is al dente comes first.

variant_of.differs: The pasta is cooked in a small amount of thick soup that it absorbs, with hot liquid added as it goes and the starch kept in the pot, not in a large pot of salted water that is drained away.
